reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about phase decomposition, precipitate formation, and their effect on fracture in CoCrFeMnNi under high strain rates, but cites no prior evidence (supporting_evidence_ids is empty). Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific kinetic and thermodynamic response of this alloy to adiabatic heating at grain boundaries, so these premises are entirely unsupported by the provided citations.
premises: High strain rate loading causes localized adiabatic heating and stress concentrations at grain boundaries in CoCrFeMnNi.
This triggers localized decomposition of the solid solution into nanoscale ordered/intermetallic precipitates at grain boundaries.
These brittle precipitates cause early intergranular crack initiation and brittle fracture.
Quasi-static loading does not produce such precipitates, and the alloy remains ductile.
